Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) flashcards, quiz and mind map from one article: real walkthrough
Stop making flashcards by hand. Google made me 60 from one article 📚

It's Gemini Notebook (the new name of NotebookLM), free at notebook.google.com:
1. New notebook, then Add sources: paste a link, upload a PDF or a YouTube video
2. In the Studio panel, tap Flashcards (there are 9 tools: Flashcards, Quiz, Mind Map, Audio Overview, Video Overview, Slide Deck, Infographic, Reports, Data Table)
3. Pro tip: type your focus in "What should the topic be?" (like "help me study for my biology exam")
4. Quiz: pick Hard and mix question types like Fill in the Blank

From ONE Wikipedia page I got 60 flashcards, a 12-question hard quiz and a mind map.

Free with a Google account (there's a usage limit). AI can make mistakes, so double-check facts.

Comment NOTES and I'll DM you my 5 best study prompts.
Send this to a friend with an exam coming up.

The screens in the video are our own animated recreation of the app.

Made with an AI voice and AI visuals.

items.caption:
Google AI Mode trip planner: free day-by-day itinerary with map and budget
Google planned my 3 days in Rome in seconds. Free, no sign-in ✈️

1. Go to google.com and tap AI Mode (it worked for me without even signing in)
2. Type: days + city + budget, like "plan a 3 day trip to Rome on a budget"
3. It groups sights by neighborhood, gives a daily budget (Rome: ~€70-120 a day, hotel not included) and maps every day
4. It even adds money tips: the ~€8 FL1 train from Fiumicino airport instead of a ~€55 taxi
5. Keep asking: "where should I eat near the Colosseum?"

Pro tip: add your style (food lover, with kids, nightlife).

AI can make mistakes: double-check opening hours and prices before you go.

Comment TRAVEL and I'll DM you my 5 best trip prompts.
Send this to a friend who is planning a trip.

The screens in the video are our own animated recreation of Google AI Mode.

Made with an AI voice and AI visuals.

items.first_comment: Try: "plan 2 days in [city] for under $100 a day, I love food markets, no museums". The more specific, the better the plan.

items.caption:
ChatGPT call script to lower your internet bill: what to say, ask for retention
Stop paying $80 for internet. Say this one sentence ChatGPT wrote 📞

1. Open chatgpt.com (it answered me without signing in)
2. Type: "I pay $[your price] a month for internet. A competitor offers $[their price]. Write the exact short phone script to get my provider to lower my bill, including what to say if they say no."
3. Call and read it: your price, their price, and that you'd rather stay
4. If they say no: "Could you transfer me to your retention department?" They may have offers regular support can't give
5. Got an offer? Ask for the exact monthly total with every fee, and how long the price lasts

If they match a $30 lower price, that's $360 a year.

No guarantee: providers don't have to lower your price, but a real competitor price gives you a reason to ask. Never type your account number or password into a chatbot.

Comment BILLS and I'll DM you the full script plus 7 more bill prompts.
